newsitem.title: GERMANY: German industry employers in crisis meeting on pay.
newsitem.headline: German industry employers in crisis meeting on pay.

text.p: Germany's Gesamtmetall employers federation planned a crisis meeting on Sunday over a regional pay deal which has undermined its efforts to impose cuts in sick pay allowed by a new law.

The Welt am Sonntag newspaper said the meeting, called at short notice at Frankfurt airport, would reject the deal struck in Lower Saxony state on Thursday as a pacesetter for pay rounds in the key metals and car industries.
Gesamtmetall has clashed with the powerful IG Metall union over its efforts to cut sick pay allowances which are the highest in Europe to 80 percent of normal wages.

The reductions are allowed under austerity laws passed by Chancellor Helmut Kohl's government this autumn to boost job creation in Germany, suffering from record post-unification unemployment of four million.

The union, which has three million members, has called several strikes to defend sick pay allowances at full wages. It declared victory on Thursday in Lower Saxony when employers guaranteed full sick pay entitlements into the next century.
IG Metall chief Klaus Zwickel called in Welt am Sonntag for the local pay deal, which covers 90,000 workers, to be agreed "quickly and without a lot of noise" countrywide.
If no deal is reached, then strike action could begin in Bavaria from March 1, when a binding pledge not to down tools expires.

Gesamtmetall is battling to contain wage costs in an industry which is losing over 100,000 jobs a year, but its hard line on sick pay has been undermined by what Welt am Sonntag called an unprecedented breaking of ranks in Lower Saxony.
